To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) CCDs are a good choice of digraphs for cluster analysis, (2) CCDs require the specification of an unknown parameter, and (3) RK-CCDs are robust clustering methods and do not require the specification of the unknown parameter.

\begin{itemize} \item RK-CCDs are a parameter free version of CCDs. \item The number of clusters in a data can be estimated from the number of connected components in the RK-CCDs of the data set, which is the same as the minimum dominating set of the RK-CCD. \item The intensity parameter can be estimated from a function that estimates the number of clusters in the data. \item The RK-CCD clustering algorithms are parameter free

(1) RK-CCDs are parameter free clustering methods, (2) RK-CCD clustering methods are robust to noise, outliers, and the choice of intensity, and (3) the proposed methods outperform some commonly used clustering methods.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and application of a parameter free clustering algorithm that estimates the number of clusters, the cluster centers and the cluster intensity parameter.
developing new clustering methods that are parameter free, and are robust to noise clusters.
the development of new clustering methods, which do not require any information on a parameter, and yet are able to estimate the number of natural clusters in the data sets.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
RK-CCDs are superior to the other methods in terms of the number of clusters estimated and the quality of the estimated clusterings.
our proposed clustering methods are superior to the other methods considered here in terms of the number of correct clusters found and the number of noise points identified.
the proposed clustering methods outperform the other density-based and prototype based clustering methods on most data sets.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the proposed algorithms are robust to the choice of intensity parameter, and are able to estimate the correct number of convex clusters in a data sets, and hence are able to produce partitions that are comparable with the state-of-the-art clustering methods.
the proposed methods are robust to the noise clusters, are able to estimate the number of true clusters, are parameter free and are computationally efficient.
the CCD algorithms and their parameter free versions are robust to noise and are competitive with the existing clustering methods.
The main takeaway from our work is that
our proposed clustering algorithms are able to estimate the number of cluster and the cluster intensity parameter simultaneously, and hence, are able to provide a robust clustering of the data set.
the proposed algorithms perform well in terms of clustering accuracy and the estimated cluster number, and are robust to noise clusters.
the CCDs and RK-CCDs can be used for robust clustering of a wide class of data sets.
